headline: Neural networks infer volumes, tilt images and atomic coordinates from cryo-EM density
label: Deep Learning For Cryo Em
summary: Learned models are now applied directly to experimental cryo-EM and cryo-ET density for reconstruction, missing-wedge completion and atomic modeling.
synthesis: The common thread is learned models operating directly on experimental cryo-EM and cryo-ET density. Cryo-SWAN applies a wavelet-inspired voxel variational autoencoder to cryo-EM volumes, reporting improved reconstruction and an organized latent space. On tomography, MW-RaMViD adapts random-mask video diffusion to generate missing tilt images for missing-wedge correction, and DeepMDTOMO uses a supervised 3D convolutional encoder-decoder to predict all-atom coordinates from subtomograms. A convolutional autoencoder with a regression network maps noisy cryo-EM particle images to atomic coordinates through latent representations. What is new is inference of volumes, tilt images and coordinates from experimental density, including missing-wedge completion. Architectures differ and all four items are preprints, so reported performance claims remain unestablished.
